title: Kernel Fallback Synthesis & Release Gating Sync
summary: Post-incident synthesis after recent kernel fallback events; align owners and gating criteria for next release; agree on short-term mitigations and a staged rollout plan with clear abort/fallback thresholds.
topics: Immediate mitigations (rate limiting, KV cache warmers)
Release gating criteria and canary thresholds

Maya to push alert tuning and set new SLO for fallback rate by Oct 10
Zoe to update release gate checklist to include fallback runbook link and test plan by Oct 12
Diego to run targeted stress tests (RUNTIME-1122) and share results in #infra-incidents
Priya to prepare stakeholder summary and customer-facing note for enterprise accounts by Oct 15

Maya Chen: Implement immediate alert threshold changes and create dashboard widget for fallback percentage (due 2025-10-10)

transcript:
Header: 2025-10-07 09:30 PDT / Duration 62m
Attendees: Owen, Maya, Priya, Diego, Zoe, Daniel, Samira, Alex, Jae
Links referenced: https://redwood.company/ops/playbooks/kernel-fallback, ticket INF-3987, RUNTIME-1122, #infra-incidents slack channel

[00:00] Owen Li: ok, thanks everyone for joining early, uh we're here to synthesize the kernel fallback incidents from last week and decide what must land before we cut the next release. we have 60 minutes, let's keep it action-oriented.
[00:21] Priya N.: quick note, timeline for the customer comms — we promised an update by mid-oct, so we need the postmortem draft this week-ish, right.
[00:33] Maya Chen: yeah, and from SRE's side, the immediate pain was a spike in fallback from 0.6% to about 6% during the traffic surge — look at INF-3987 for the traces. some of the traces show the runtime kernel selectors falling back to a slower emulation path, maybe due to heap fragmentation on the GPU or driver hiccup.
[00:58] Diego Alvarez: i dug into the kernel logs, there were a couple of failed cuLaunchKernel calls and then our runtime detected incompatible kernel and switched to the generic path. there were also some memory eviction loops - the k v cache warmers didn't hold. might be a combination of the new attention optimization + specific sequence length distribution.
[01:20] Samira Khan: so is this tied to the new quantized kernel we rolled three days ago? or is this an unrelated orchestration issue?
[01:28] Diego Alvarez: i don't think it's purely quantization. the quantized kernels were exercised, yes, but the failures seem tied to driver timing and memory fragmentation. still, quantized paths make different scheduling choices so they may have increased memory pressure.
[01:45] Daniel Park: ok, pragmatic - what are immediate mitigations?
[01:49] Maya Chen: immediate: 1) reduce canary traffic to 10% for affected models, 2) bump retry window in the router so we don't cascade load, 3) enable a temporary throttle on max batch size for 12 hours, and 4) restart a subset of GPU hosts to clear fragmentation. all of which are low-risk and reversible.
[02:18] Zoe Park: restarting hosts could impact throughput; we should schedule a rolling restart with capacity guardrails. If we do that during business hours we need comms to on-call.
[02:30] Owen Li: agreed. also add a fallback runbook link to the release gating checklist so PMs can't accidentally push. Zoe, can you own adding that?
[02:38] Zoe Park: yes, i will.
[02:40] [00:03:00] Priya N.: a quick cross-check — does security need to be looped in? Jae?
[03:08] Jae Kim: for now it's not a data breach vector; it's availability. i want the postmortem to include whether any attempts were made to access host-level metrics that shouldn't be exposed. otherwise SOC two compliance note — keep logs for 90 days.
[03:28] Diego Alvarez: one weirdness — in a few traces the kernel selector mis-identified model dimensions, there was a mismatch between the compiled kernel metadata and the runtime's model metadata after a model swap. ticket RUNTIME-1122 captures that. seems like a bug in our model hot-swap path.
[03:56] Owen Li: is that reproducible in staging?
[04:01] Diego Alvarez: partially. i can repro with a narrow sequence: run model A for long sequences then hot-swap to model B with shorter seqs while runners are near memory capacity. it's flaky tho.
[04:20] Maya Chen: reproducibility is key for the release gate. if Diego can produce a deterministic repro, we can add the test to the canary suite.
[04:33] Diego Alvarez: i'll prioritize that for tomorrow.
[04:36] [00:05:00] Priya N.: on gating criteria — Zoe, what are the current canary thresholds?
[04:45] Zoe Park: currently we check error rate < 0.5%, latency med < SLA, and p95 token latency ramp. i propose adding fallback-rate < 1% over a 30m window for canaries, and an abort if fallback-rate >5% sustained for 1h.
[05:05] Samira Khan: those numbers sound right, but can we make them model-specific? some large LMs will always show higher baseline fallback due to big KV caches.
[05:16] Owen Li: make them model-specific, yes. default to conservative thresholds and allow calibrations per model. Priya, that's a PM task for the rollout docs.
[05:27] Priya N.: noted.
[05:30] [00:10:00] Daniel Park: what's the monitoring work? i heard alerts fired late.
[05:36] Maya Chen: our alert was based on generic error-rate which didn't catch kernel fallback specifically. we need a dedicated metric for "kernel_fallback_count" and a derived "fallback_rate" by model and region. also need a dashboard tile in Console for quick triage.
[05:56] Diego Alvarez: we can instrument runtime to emit a telemetry event when fallback happens with fields: model_id, seq_len, batch_size, kernel_name, host_id. that will help cluster-level correlation.
[06:12] Owen Li: good. Diego, add those telemetry fields and wire them into the log pipeline.
[06:18] Diego Alvarez: will do. ETA: 48 hours.
[06:22] [00:15:00] Maya Chen: also, we should tune retries at the router layer to avoid retry storms. that was a secondary amplification last time. reduce immediate retries and add jitter.
[06:40] Zoe Park: canary rollout plan: 1) internal canary 5% traffic in us-west for 6h, observe fallback rate and p95, 2) increase to 15% if stable for 24h, 3) regional expansion next week. abort if fallback-rate >5% sustained 1h.
[06:58] Samira Khan: do we have load test coverage for these sequences?
[07:04] Diego Alvarez: current synthetic load doesn't mirror the long-tail sequences we saw. i'll expand the stress matrix with seq patterns and batch combos.
[07:13] [00:20:00] Priya N.: comms: once we have a postmortem draft, we'll share with enterprise accounts and update status page. do not call this a data incident; it's availability.
[07:26] Jae Kim: confirm — add SOC two note in postmortem and retention plan.
[07:33] Owen Li: ok, to be explicit on owners and due dates — Maya, Diego, Zoe, Priya — we spelled out tasks. anyone else?
[07:41] Daniel Park: i'd like a runbook entry that includes an automated failover to older kernel variant if fallback spike detected. is that feasible?
[07:51] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can ship an automated toggle in the router that prefers the older kernel variant for specific model_id when background fallback exceeds threshold. that'll take some code and an integration test. estimate 1 sprint.
[08:08] Zoe Park: include that in medium-term mitigations; do not block the immediate release on it.
[08:14] [00:30:00] Priya N.: ok, open questions: 1) repro in staging? Diego says partial. 2) telemetry fields to be added? Diego doing 48h. 3) updates to canary thresholds? Zoe doing by Oct 12. 4) postmortem draft? Owen doing by Oct 14.
[08:33] Maya Chen: i will also add a short-term dashboard and temporary alert rules by Oct 10.
[08:40] Owen Li: good. any objections to the proposed canary numbers? silence — assume consensus.
[08:46] Samira Khan: one more ask — let's run the stress tests with both quant and fp16 paths, to make sure quantization isn't an orthogonal factor.
[08:58] Diego Alvarez: noted, will include quant and fp16 in the matrix.
[09:05] [00:40:00] Owen Li: wrap-up: we have owners, timelines, and gating updates. Priya will coordinate comms. Zoe adds runbook and gating. Diego does repro & stress. Maya tunes alerts and dashboard. Owen drafts postmortem.
[09:22] Priya N.: can we meet briefly next week for status? same time Tuesday?
[09:26] Owen Li: yes, tentatively Tue 09:30. i'll send invite.
[09:31] Zoe Park: i'll add the checklist item and the abort threshold.
[09:35] Daniel Park: thanks everyone, appreciate the focus.
[09:38] [End of transcript]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache), some overlapping speech flagged, timestamps approximate.
